newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says strong pound damaging exports.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says strong pound damaging exports.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday the strong pound was damaging exports and would restrain manufacturing activity.
"The difference of opinion between myself and the Bank (of England) ... is I think we should have strong regard for the strength of the pound," Clarke said in a talk show on BBC television.
"It's damaging our exports and it will restrain our manufacturing activity. Putting up interest rates against that background -- I don't think it's the time to do it," he said.
Clarke said he thought Bank of England governor Eddie George thought he put a little too much emphasis on the strength of the pound, while he thought George put too little emphasis on this.
The Bank has said it would prefer interest rates to rise from their present six percent level to cut off inflationary pressures in the economy.
Clarke sees a strong pound deflating the economy and argues higher interest rates will merely increase buying interest in sterling.
